pest.title:
Pest Details
& Treatment Guide
pest.name: Brown Plant Hopper
pest.summary: A major pest of rice crops, primarily damaging plants by extracting sap from the phloem. Severe infestations cause "hopperburn," where plants turn yellow and dry up rapidly.
pest.step1Body: Remove standing water from the field for 3-4 days to reduce humidity at the base of the plants.
pest.step2Body: Apply recommended systemic insecticides if hopper population exceeds the economic threshold level.
pest.step3Body: Regularly check the base of rice stems for nymphs and adults to assess treatment effectiveness.
pest.measure1Body: Cultivate BPH-resistant rice varieties suitable for your region.
pest.measure2Body: Avoid excessive use of nitrogen fertilizers which promote lush growth attractive to hoppers.

gemini.emptyTitle: How can I help you today?
gemini.emptyBody: Upload a photo of your plant or describe the symptoms to get AI-powered agricultural advice.
gemini.label: Ask Gemini
gemini.sampleQuestion: My tomato plants have these strange brown spots with yellow halos on the lower leaves. What could it be?
gemini.sampleAnswer: Those symptoms match early blight. Remove the affected lower leaves, avoid overhead watering, and mulch around the base to stop soil splashing onto the plant.

comments.title: Comments
comments.c1Body: I've noticed some unusual yellowing on my rice leaves this season. Could it be a deficiency?
comments.c2Body: Looks like nitrogen deficiency to me. Have you applied urea recently? The pattern is very typical for this stage of growth.
comments.c3Body: I agree with Rahim, but also check for soil moisture levels. Sometimes poor drainage can mimic these symptoms before true deficiency sets in.
comments.c4Body: Drainage is good, I'll definitely look into the nitrogen levels. Thanks both!
